findings.reason: the section must name the grid record's reader in `eddb.py` (or state that the loader reuses one), so the store keeps a single reader/writer owner.
findings.text: §6 adds a grid record writer to `eddb.py` "beside `write_channel`" under the shared `{shot}.zarr/{category}/{name}` layout, but names no symmetric grid reader: `eddb.py` owns the store and reads every channel through `read_channel` (eddb.py:280), yet the SELENE loader is only said to "turn the cached record into an `EfitLabels`" with no reader named, so the plan can land a store whose writer lives in `eddb.py` while its reader opens zarr directly — the exact second-owner drift `channel_path` was introduced to prevent

findings.reason: the section should name the added `BatchResult` field and its header section, so the shared envelope's change is explicit rather than implied.
findings.text: §6's EQDB refusal is "carried in the same `BatchResult` beside the channel refusals" and `encode_batch`/`decode_batch` gain the EQDB framing, but `BatchResult` today is exactly `records: list[ChannelRecord]` + `refusals: list[ChannelRefusal]` (eddb_remote.py:121-131) and its docstring says the two fields partition the requests, so the third refusal kind forces a third field and a new envelope section the section does not name while asserting it "retires nothing"; with the week's four families all reading 0, this is the one place the section adds shared-contract surface without accounting for it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the additions extend deep modules behind their existing interfaces (`eddb_remote`'s extractor dispatch, `eddb`'s single store, `transform_engine`'s resolver, `spine_bench`'s shot-set/parity tables) rather than fanning complexity across new shallow wrappers; the plan's own §6 rejects the two thin alternatives (a parallel EDDB reader, a re-derived field-per-ampere relation).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the store's write owner is named (`eddb.py channel_path` / `write_channel`) but the grid record's read side names no owner, so the EQDB store risks a second reader beside `eddb.py read_channel`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — supplied counts public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §6's EQDB addition states what it retires but does not name the added shared-structure surface on `BatchResult`/the batch envelope, only the new record type.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the open sections name the machinery they extend and every citation I opened resolves: COCOS factors via `cocos.py:63 canonical_factor`, the probe-angle supplier via `description_reader.py:253` `read_geometry_table`'s `probe_angle_source` branch, the machine registry via `machine_identity.py:145 default_registry`, the SELENE-comparison seat via `efit_referee.py:120 read_efit_geometry(loader=...)` and `equilibrium_labels.py:465 build_geometry_from_arrays`; no subsystem is rebuilt that already exists.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one wrapper-shaped proposal, §6's EQDB request/record types beside `ChannelRequest`/`ChannelRecord`, states why the channel types cannot be widened (an EQDB request is keyed `(shot, record)` and answers a 2D psi grid, not a `(channel, time)` array) and keeps the extractor's refusal and `SshTransport` contract, so it is an extension of the owner rather than a parallel path.
